title: The SRC speaks with one determinative voice while preserving individual dissent on the public record
content:
A.6.1.1.1.3.1.4.3.1.1 requires the SRC conclusion to "reflect the majority opinion of SRC members," then immediately adds that "individual SRC members are free to post dissenting or concurring opinions at their discretion," elaborated at A.6.1.1.1.3.1.4.9.1.

The split is between two things a review body produces. The **decision** must be single-valued, because it gates a binary outcome — the proposal advances or it does not. The **reasoning** need not be, and compressing it to a majority position would destroy information that holders and future reviewers can use.

With a three-seat Council, this is load-bearing rather than decorative. Every contested determination is 2–1, and without a dissent channel a 2–1 block and a 3–0 block look identical from outside. A published dissent tells holders that a serious objection to the reasoning exists inside the body that has veto power over them, which is the only signal available given they cannot overturn the outcome.

Dissent is also the main accountability mechanism against the Council's own failure modes. A.6.1.1.1.3.1.4.10 makes "blocking valid proposals due to malicious intent or evident poor due diligence" a removal ground — a charge that is far easier to substantiate when one member has already put the argument against the majority in writing at the time.
description: Conclusions reflect the majority opinion, but members may post concurring or dissenting opinions to the Sky Forum, separating the binding decision from the reasoning available to holders.
